nota: Portada del refresh «Pipeline de ventas en HubSpot» (post 246045). Fórmula nueva (operador, 2026-10-25): sin persona al frente y sin vidrio, como SEO y AEO (MCB-AEO1-169) y Loop (MCB-LOOP1-169). El pipeline como fenómeno físico: tres umbrales de luz en fila son las etapas; de un grupo de bloques, cada umbral deja pasar menos, y sólo uno cruza el último. Lo que avanza no es lo que se empuja, es lo que cumple el criterio de salida. Excepción de alcance: §2 caso 4 define Manzanitas por persona; esta portada va sin personas por la fórmula nueva.

escena: SCENE (cinematic still, Hollywood drama, a vast dark contemporary room at night, a faint trace of haze only on the right of the frame, a cool frame, no people anywhere): a photograph looking well DOWN onto a long matte black table from a high angle, the camera raised high above the near end of the table, about forty-five degrees above the table plane, never at table height, about three metres from the arrangement, 85mm f/4, focused on the lone block. The far edge of the table crosses the frame about one sixth of the way down from the top; beyond it the dark floor of the room falls away. Far from the camera, on the far part of the table, stands a small arrangement that runs straight AWAY from the lens, along the length of the table: exactly THREE low GATES, one behind another. Each gate is a slim matte black metal frame, a low doorway about half as tall as it is wide, standing across the table and facing the camera. A thin light hidden under its top bar shines straight down and lays one narrow band of azure-white light (#0375DB and cold white) across the tabletop exactly on the threshold, with soft edges: the light falls on the table; the frame itself does not glow. The gates are NOT neon, NOT glowing tubes, NOT rings or frames of light, NOT portals, NOT holograms, NOT a tunnel. The gates stand about a hand-width apart, far enough that, seen from this high camera, each gate appears whole and entirely ABOVE the one in front of it in the photograph, with dark tabletop between them: they never overlap and never nest inside one another like a tunnel. Small identical BLOCKS stand on the table along that row: each one a low rectangular block of dark graphite-anodized aluminium, a little longer than it is wide and about half as tall, with crisp machined edges and smooth matte faces, about a quarter of the width of a gate; they are never dice, never dominoes, never game pieces, never toy blocks, and carry NO pips, NO dots, NO numbers, NO letters, NO marks. In FRONT of the first gate, nearest the camera, exactly FOUR blocks stand side by side in one straight row across the table, as wide as the gate. Between the first and the second gate, exactly THREE blocks stand side by side in one row. Between the second and the third gate, exactly TWO blocks stand side by side. BEYOND the third gate stands exactly ONE block, alone, centred. Every row runs across the table, never one block behind another, so every block is seen separately. Count them: four, three, two, one; ten blocks, three gates. MOMENT, the exact moment it happens: the lone block has just crossed the third threshold and come to rest a finger-width beyond its band of light; the spotlight has just found it, while the two blocks behind it still wait on the near side. The whole arrangement is FAR from the camera and SMALL in the frame: its widest part, the first gate with its row of four, is only about one sixteenth of the frame width. It stands inside the right third of the frame: its left edge a little past two thirds of the way across from the left edge, its right edge well short of three quarters of the way across, its centre about seven tenths of the way across. From the row of four to the lone block it climbs the frame from about the middle of the frame height up to about one quarter from the top. The lone block beyond the last gate is the brightest object in the frame: the narrow spotlight from above falls only on it, and its top face glows clean cold white with crisp edges. The only colour in the frame is the azure of the bands of light at the gates; there is no pink, no magenta and no other colour. Each row of waiting blocks stands just in front of the next band of light, so that band catches the front faces of its blocks with a thin azure edge; the lone block is still far brighter; the row of four, nearest the camera, falls softly out of focus and into shadow. There is no face anywhere in this frame: wherever the lighting notes speak of a face, they mean the lone lit block beyond the last gate. There is no hand, no person, no device, no screen, no glass, no cards, no arrows, no lines drawn on the table, no grid, no game board, no tracks, no conveyor belt. The bare matte black tabletop fills the whole lower half of the frame as one calm, even, dark surface receding toward the arrangement. Between the left edge of the frame and the arrangement there is a wide band of empty darkness about two thirds of the frame wide; every lit thing stays inside the right third of the frame. Above the table, the LEFT 64 % of the frame is calm, deep dark space: no light and no objects, no bokeh, no beams. The haze is so faint that only the spotlight draws a visible shaft: one thin vertical shaft of cold white light straight down onto the lone block, inside the right third of the frame; the gates show their light only as bands on the table; nothing of it leans toward the left of the frame. The materials are contemporary and well kept: matte black tabletop with a fine even surface, crisp graphite-anodized aluminium blocks, slim matte black metal gates with no visible cables, no dust, no wear, nothing vintage, nothing warm, amber or golden, no tungsten glow. The whole frame is cool and contemporary. No books, no lamps, no plants, no papers, no monitors. Enormous contrast, no readable text anywhere, no logos of any brand.
